2025.crop: Small: rarely more than 30 hl/ha in either colour (Inside Burgundy); third small crop in five years (Vinetur).

2026.note: Very early, very hot vintage: historic May heatwave, June/July heat peaks of 38-40°C, heat sums ahead of 2003 by mid-July; very small, juiceless berries. No published chart scores yet.
2026.harvest_src: Burgundy Report harvest diary: Benoît Ente picked a Puligny 1er cru on 8 Aug; general (mainly Chardonnay) picking under way 12-13 Aug, including some young-vine reds; de Vogüé picking Musigny on 18 Aug (https://www.burgundy-report.com/category/harvests/vintage-2026/). A retailer report claims Montrachet picking from 13 Aug, "earliest recorded" (https://www.burgundywine.com/blog/burgundy-2026-an-exceptionally-early-harvest-but-plenty-to-be-excited-about/).
2026.crop: Very small: reds often 50-70% below normal, Corton-Charlemagne about 26 hl/ha; Bourgogne Aujourd'hui calls it the fifth short crop in seven years.

events.severity: Winter cold killed vines on the low, humid ground west of the old RN74; Morris notes the same vineyards were killed again in December 2009.

Rain into September caused a high incidence of grey rot.
Severe frost seriously reduced the potential crop.
Hail; localised crop losses (Decanter: Chambolle, Morey and Gevrey badly affected by the 1991 hail).
Second hailstorm; localised losses.
Heavy late-spring/early-summer rain caused major mildew; some growers lost crops early.
Major hail in Meursault: little wine made from Charmes, Genevrières and Perrières (Decanter: hail in May).
Major hailstorm on Puligny and part of Meursault.
Heavy rain from 10 Sep through the harvest diluted ripe grapes; rot where growers waited.
Easter Monday frost (-8°C) followed by sun badly damaged the more advanced Chardonnay; small crop in both colours.
Oïdium attack after poor June weather, worse on Chardonnay.
August heatwave with highs over 40°C scorched grapes.
Cool rain in early September brought rot, saved by a dry spell 16-26 Sep.
Storm with heavy rain and some hail on the southern Côte de Beaune; rot in Côte de Beaune reds 10-40% (Decanter).
Devastating hail on Volnay, especially the premiers crus; lesser damage in Meursault and southern Pommard.
Severe drought; hosepipe ban in the Côte d'Or until November.
Pre-harvest storm; hail damage in parts of Gevrey and Marsannay only.
Snow on 10 April, -5°C on the 11th; mostly white-wine vineyards on cooler sites affected.
Hailstorm after the early flowering.
Every day 4-13 Aug above 40°C; harvest opened 19 Aug; yields down a third to a half (Decanter).
Cool, cloudy early July led to oïdium all summer.
One of the two worst storms of a hail-ridden summer, affecting almost every village except Nuits-St-Georges.
Hard hail that wiped out swathes of these villages (Decanter); Nuits-St-Georges largely unscathed (Inside Burgundy).
Early-season hail; no effect on quality.
Very serious storm doing a great deal of damage.
Rainfall far below average all summer; drought hit young vines and thin soils.
Major hailstorm, especially around Griotte- and Chapelle-Chambertin.
Hail damage in St-Aubin En Remilly.
Hail on parts of Beaune; Decanter also notes hail in parts of Montrachet and Chassagne.
Grey, cool summer; rot in the red vineyards by August, sorting reduced yields by about 20% (Decanter).
Cool, wet May-June; mildew, oïdium and later rot all relatively rife.
Hail, worst in Savigny; up to 70% of the crop lost in places (Decanter); whole swathes wiped out in Meursault.
Ascension Day hail, especially on the grands crus.
Below -20°C before Christmas killed vines on low ground west of the old RN74 (first time since 1985).
Heavy hail; the storm also "turned" near-ripe white grapes, causing rot in Chassagne and to a lesser extent Puligny and Meursault.
End-of-June heat near 40°C grilled some grapes.
Hail on the southern Côte de Beaune (and devastating in Rully); reduced potential yields in these villages (Drouhin).
Clear-dawn frost damage (also in Chablis).
Second, localised frost.
Downpour with hail during flowering (Decanter dates it 6 June); mostly leaves damaged.
Rain through June into July; significant mildew and oïdium.
Sudden heat spike grilled exposed bunches.
Hail across almost all Côte de Beaune appellations; up to 80% of the harvest damaged in Puligny, Meursault and Volnay (Drouhin); yields often 15 hl/ha or less.
Severe hail over about 1,400 ha (Drouhin; Decanter says 1,300 ha); Clos des Mouches had no crop at all; second year running for these parcels.
Warm, misty, wet harvest weather let rot gallop, especially in late-picked whites.
Several waves of hail; hailed vines gave 5-10% of a normal crop (Drouhin); many producers lost about half their crop (Decanter).
Drosophila suzukii plague caused acetic (sour) rot; some Côte de Nuits plots picked early.
The only Côte d'Or hail of the year; small damage.
Exceptionally dry, hot summer; July heatwave shut vines down, delaying véraison in the Côte de Nuits.

Night of 26-27 April; Côte de Beaune worst. Yield falls: Marsannay -44/-46/-65% (red/white/rosé), Chambolle -39% (Musigny -55%), Chorey/Ladoix/Pernand/Savigny a third to a half, Chassagne -24%, Chambertin -39% (Inside Burgundy); Rousseau lost two-thirds, DRC -50% (Decanter); Montrachet: six domaines pooled grapes for two barrels.
Strong mildew pressure through May-June added to the frost losses; organic growers forced to use other treatments.

Minor hail damage.

Light hail without real consequences.
July storms; genuinely damaging hail only in southern Nuits-St-Georges and Côte-de-Nuits Villages.
One of the three hottest seasons since 1945 (with 1947, behind 2003); sunburn sorting needed.
Frost on 4-5 April (again 12-15 April, lighter); low-lying Côte de Beaune lost up to 60% (Lafarge, Decanter); Pernand lost nearly half its crop to frost plus poor flowering.
Last week of June up to 40°C, first of two severe heatwaves; vignerons estimated about 10% of the crop lost to each heatwave (Decanter).
Hail without too much damage.
Hail with rain; limited damage (further limited hail on 8 June in Chambolle and Gevrey).
Limited hail damage.
Almost no rain from mid-March to end April and an extreme water deficit in July; leaves dying and skins shrivelling by mid-August.
Heat spike at véraison turning into a late-evening hailstorm on the southern side of Nuits-St-Georges.
Arctic air 6-8 April, down to -8°C after snow; Chardonnay worst hit with 50-100% losses (Drouhin); Burgundy crop about half normal.
From 8-9 May, intense mildew pressure into summer; rot and oïdium at harvest.
Storm with hail in the first days of May.
Warmest, driest, sunniest year on record; August heat peaks 8-13 Aug and 24-25 Aug.
Damp April to mid-May gave considerable mildew pressure, generally managed.
Hail on some plots without significant damage.
Mild hail in the early morning.
Evening storm with some damage along a track from St-Aubin over Blagny to Meursault; mitigated by the large crop.
35-36°C on 18-24 Aug (slight sunburn) and heat again during the September harvest.
Cold snap 18-23 April; limited Côte d'Or damage, mainly chardonnay; Drouhin says the southern Côte de Beaune was hit more severely.
Vicious mildew in May-June, worst on waterlogged low-lying vineyards that could not be sprayed; attacked bunches and wood.
Hailstorm (Drouhin reports further hail in the Côte d'Or from May to early August).
Many June days above 35°C, occasionally near 40°C.
About ten days of heatwave from 8 Aug; grapes gained about three degrees of potential alcohol in a week (Fontaine-Gagnard); young vines stressed.
Historic May heatwave (weekly mean 10°C above normal), then June/July peaks of 38-40°C with tropical nights; heat sum ahead of 2003 by 12 July.
Hail during a cool spell after flowering: damaged grapelets in the Côte de Beaune (photos from Volnay grower Nicolas Rossignol); a minute of small hail in Premeaux with no visible damage.
Storms on 15 and 18 July; Marsannay badly hit, potentially 60% of an already half-sized crop lost.
Significant water stress in the Côte de Beaune after a dry late spring; northern Côte de Nuits driest zone into July.

method: Consensus = median of the available published chart values after converting each to a 50-100 Parker-style scale, rounded half up. Conversions: Wine Advocate and Wine Spectator are already 100-point and used as is (ranges such as 92-95 take the midpoint; the WA maturity letter is dropped). Berry Bros & Rudd 1-10 -> 60 + 4n (10=100, 9=96, 8=92, 7=88, 6=84, 5=80, 4=76). Decanter stars out of 5 -> 60 + 7.2 x stars (5=96, 4.5=92.4, 4=88.8, 3.5=85.2, 3=81.6, 2.5=78, 2=74.4). The BBR and Decanter linear maps were calibrated by eye against the WA/WS 100-point scores of the same years (e.g. BBR 7 and Decanter 4 years average about 88-90 on WA/WS; BBR 5/Decanter 3 about 80-83). Scope caveats: only WA and WS (from 1995) split reds by Côte de Nuits / Côte de Beaune; BBR "Red Burgundy", Decanter "Côte d'Or red" and WS "older vintage reds" (1985-1994) are applied to both red cells. For whites, WA "Burgundy (White)", WS "Burgundy white" and BBR "White Burgundy" cover all of Burgundy (incl. Chablis/Mâconnais); Decanter's Côte d'Or white rating is used where given (2005-2019) and its general white-Burgundy rating before that. Decanter ratings stop at 2019 and are missing for 2014-2015 reds and 2008 whites; WS reds stop at 2023 and whites at 2024; WA has 2025 as "not tested". Charts that could not be used: Jancis Robinson (Cloudflare-blocked, and its chart is narrative without scores), Vinous, Burghound, Jasper Morris/Inside Burgundy (free vintage overviews but no numeric vintage ratings; used for notes, events and harvest dates), BIVB and bourgogne-wines.com (connection refused through the proxy). A cell with fewer than 2 sources is flagged estimate:true (only 2025); its score is a judgement from harvest reports, not the single BBR value. "converted" lists each source value after conversion. Drink hints are derived from the WA maturity letter (T hold, E drink or hold, R drink now, I irregular, C past peak) and WS "Past peak" labels, with a few hand overrides (premature oxidation for 1996/1999/2002 whites, BIVB advice for 2024). Harvest dates: the observed Labbé et al. 2019 Beaune series is not in the article supplement (it has only reconstructed GHD and temperatures; observed data are on the Euro-Climhist platform, not downloadable here), so harvest_start uses the ban des vendanges or general start of picking in the Côte de Beaune from Inside Burgundy, Decanter and Maison Joseph Drouhin vintage reports, and for 1985-1989 and 1995 the Burgundy regional composite of the Daux et al. 2012 grape-harvest-date database (NOAA), which is approximate.
